messages:
anya: Pager: high generation latency in eu-west and ap-southeast observed at 13:02 UTC. Alerts triggered for gen-service (p95 > 2s) and queue depth rising. tagging oncall.
oncall-bot: @pager rota notification -> sam is on-call (ESCALATION: 2m). Pager report: gen-service-eu, error-rate low, latency high, affected model variants: small-gen-v1, fastgen-v2.
sam: Looking. Can someone confirm whether this is deploy or infra?
laura: Not a deploy on our side. I see elevated GPU utilization on the eu cluster and a bunch of long-running KV-cache priming requests.
jordan: Observing CPU spikes on the routing plane too. Some requests are getting routed repeatedly. Routing logs: `ERROR route: failed to acquire worker` repeated.
anya: I'm drafting a status update. Quick customer-impact check: which customers are behind dedicated capacity in eu-west?
mike: Two customers on dedicated pools: AcmeCorp (prod) and NovusHealth (staging). Hosted customers see degraded tail latency (~200ms extra p95). No 5xx.
sam: Good, so impact: increased latency only, no errors. Draft initial status: "We are investigating increased generation latency affecting EU/APAC regions. Some customers may experience slower responses. We are prioritizing routing and cache warmup. No data loss or 5xx errors observed."
anya: Paste first draft here, will refine. Also flag SLA impact? If p95 degraded past SLA threshold for >5m for a customer on Dedicated, we need to notify support and billing.
jordan: AcmeCorp p95 is 2.8s vs SLA 2s for a 10-minute window. We should flag for billing ops.
laura: Ops runbook step: try draining the hot worker set and reseed with a fresh pool to clear the KV priming backlog. Command: ```sh
# drain workers in eu-west pool
redwoodctl pool drain --region eu-west --pool gen-hot-01
sleep 30
redwoodctl pool scale --region eu-west --pool gen-hot-01 --size 4
```
sam: Doing drain now. I'll monitor tracing for routing loops.
ops_bot: Runbook action logged: drain started by sam at 13:06 UTC.
anya: Statuspage draft (initial):
> We are investigating increased generation latency impacting EU and APAC regions. Responses may be slower than usual; some customers on dedicated pools may see degraded p95 latency. No request failures or data loss. Engineers are actively mitigating. Next update in 20 minutes or sooner.
laura: Add affected model names and regions to be explicit: small-gen-v1, fastgen-v2; regions: eu-west, ap-southeast-1.
sam: Update posted to internal #incidents-drafts for review. Please approve copy or suggest changes.
mike: Customer-facing one-liner suggestion: "We're experiencing slower-than-normal responses in EU and APAC. Our engineers are resolving this — no data loss. Expected next update in ~20 minutes."
anya: @jordan can you confirm whether this crosses any contractual SLA windows?
jordan: Confirmed for AcmeCorp — open an SLA incident ticket. I can start the ticket.
anya: Internal comms checklist (quick):
- [ ] Pager acknowledged (sam)
- [x] Initial status drafted
- [ ] Status reviewed by SRE (jordan/laura)
- [ ] Customer notification prepared for AcmeCorp (support + AM)
- [ ] Billing/SLA team alerted (jordan)
- [ ] Postmortem owner assigned

laura: After drain, we're seeing queue depth decrease. Tail p95 improving to 1.6s in eu-west after 2 minutes.
sam: Nice. I'll keep routing logs open for 10 more minutes. If stable, we can prepare a follow-up status: partial mitigation.
anya: Draft update (10m):
> Update: We implemented worker pool drain and reseed in EU which has reduced queue depth and improved latency for most customers. Some residual tail latency remains in APAC while caches warm. We continue to monitor; no service degradation beyond latency has been detected.
mike: For customer notification to AcmeCorp (AM draft):
> Hi team — we detected elevated generation latency affecting EU regions beginning at ~13:02 UTC. Our mitigation (worker reseed) has improved latency; we will notify you once fully resolved. No requests lost. Apologies for the disruption.
sam: Ready to publish initial + the 10m update to statuspage? Who will click publish?
anya: I'll publish the initial now and follow with the update in 10. Steps: 1) open status.redwood.ai/incidents -> new incident -> paste initial -> set impacted regions EU/APAC -> mark 'degraded performance' -> publish.
ops_bot: Statuspage draft saved by anya.
anya: Published initial status at 13:12 UTC. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/rc-2305123456
laura: Monitoring shows steady improvement. If p95 holds <2.0s for next 5m, we can post resolved.
jordan: SLA ticket opened and assigned to billing ops.
anya: Resolved draft (if stable after 7m):
> Resolved: We implemented mitigations (worker reseed and routing stabilizations) which restored normal generation latency across affected regions. No data loss occurred. We are conducting a post-incident review to identify root cause and prevent recurrence.
mike: Add follow-up note about next steps: scheduled postmortem + retention of traces for 30 days.
sam: p95 stable at 1.5s for 8m. I'm comfortable closing.
anya: Publishing resolved now. Resolved at 13:27 UTC. ops_bot: Statuspage update published by anya at 13:27 UTC.
laura: Postmortem owner: sam. Will include timeline, root cause hypothesis (KV cache priming + routing lock contention), mitigation steps and permanent fix plan.
anya: Thanks everyone. Filing internal comms: paste incident summary to #incidents-archive and DM AMs for AcmeCorp and NovusHealth with the customer message.
ops_bot: Incident closed. Duration: 00:25:00. Incident ID: rc-2305123456."
